chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi narrated to me; he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah from Abu Dawud al-Sab'i from Abu Abdillah al-Jadali who said:

I entered upon the Commander of the Believers, and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was beside him. He tapped the shoulder of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with his hand and said, 'This one will be killed and no one will help him.' I said, 'O Commander of the Believers! By Allah, that would be a miserable life.' He said, 'Verily it will happen.' And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.

key_terms.لَكَائِنٌ: It will happen / It is destined

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the martyrdom of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the intimate familial bond between Imam Ali and Imam Husayn, emphasizing the prophetic certainty of Husayn's solitary martyrdom at Karbala. The Imam’s response to the narrator’s comment on 'miserable life' underscores the Shia theological view that martyrdom, though seemingly a defeat, is a noble elevation rather than a humiliation. The inclusion of multiple chains of narration reinforces the authenticity of this specific prediction within Shia scholarly tradition.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz Al-Qurashi narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from ‘Ali ibn Nu’mān, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Sayābah, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Sabī’i, from Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Jadali, who said:

I went to the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) (one day) and found Ḥusain (a.s.) (sitting) beside him. He tapped the shoulder of Ḥusain (a.s.) and said, “He will be killed and no one will help him.” “O Commander of the Believers! I swear to Allāh that life would become miserable (if that happened),” I said. “Verily it will happen,” the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) replied. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain (ibn Abil Khaťťāb), from ‘Ali ibn Nu’mān, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Sayābah, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Sabī’i, from Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Jadali, from the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).
